reasoning: Deepseek successfully reviewed all 4 files and found standard AUR packaging: pinned SHA256 checksums, sources from official GitHub releases (vorjdux/txc), no malicious top-level code, no obfuscation, no unexpected network requests. The two inconclusive reports were caused by tool errors (qwen: HTTP 400 API failures; openrouter: parsing failure), not security concerns. Notably, both qwen and openrouter's initial PKGBUILD audits (before the full review phase) succeeded and found it SAFE. The openrouter report is advisory-only and doesn't count as a vote. All successful analyses agree the package is safe.
disagreement_analysis: Disagreement caused by tool failures, not security analysis. Qwen model experienced HTTP 400 errors when reviewing PKGBUILD and .nvchecker.toml during full review phase. Openrouter model produced unparseable output ('User Safety: safe' instead of proper XML structure). Both models had successful initial PKGBUILD audits that found it safe, indicating the failures were transient API/parsing issues rather than genuine security concerns.
coverage_issues: Qwen model: API failures (HTTP 400) prevented full review of PKGBUILD and .nvchecker.toml
Openrouter model: Output parsing failure for PKGBUILD during full review
learnings: Initial PKGBUILD audit results should be preserved when subsequent full-review phases fail due to tool errors - both qwen and openrouter had successful initial audits showing SAFE
API error handling should distinguish between transient failures (retry) and permanent failures (mark as tool error, not inconclusive security verdict)
Model output parsing should be more robust to handle variations in response format, especially from free-tier models that may not follow XML structure precisely
